about: The corporate-sector catalog: long-record anchors for the history layer (US only) and the modern micro layer for the bridge and the live cone. Status: pulled (the workflow fetched it), planned (a route exists, not yet landed), attach (has to be supplied as a file). Provenance class per the history README: counted (self-reported, audited, lagged) for filings; measured/compiled for the national accounts.

entries.title: Financial Accounts of the United States (Z.1), nonfinancial corporate business: debt securities and loans, corporate equities at market value, net worth, total liabilities, capital expenditures, net dividends, liquid assets; BEA corporate profits (annual 1929-, quarterly 1947-); nominal GDP
entries.coverage: US, quarterly from 1945Q4 (Z.1), annual from 1929 (BEA profits)
entries.retrieval: workflow: FRED API with FRED_API_KEY; series resolved by exact title at run time, ids recorded in raw/FRED-Z1/series_used.json
entries.license: public domain (Federal Reserve Board, BEA); FRED terms of use
entries.provenance_class: compiled (sector balance sheets built from reports and surveys; profits from tax and survey data)
feeds: us_corporate_annual.csv: nonfinancial corporate debt/GDP, equity market value/GDP, net worth growth, capex/GDP, dividends/profits, liquid assets/debt, profits/GDP (1929-)

entries.status: pulled; current workbook supplied by hand 2026-11-06 (to 2026-10)
entries.title: Robert Shiller, US stock market data 1871-: S&P composite price, dividends, earnings, CPI, long rate, real series and CAPE (monthly)
entries.retrieval: workflow: shillerdata.com (xls link on the page), with the Yale address as fallback
entries.license: posted for public use with attribution (Irrational Exuberance data)
entries.provenance_class: compiled (Cowles Commission back to 1871, S&P since 1926; earnings and dividends are the index's reported aggregates)
feeds: us_corporate_annual.csv: CAPE, real earnings growth 1y/3y, real price growth 3y, earnings yield minus the long rate
entries.note: the Yale server serves a copy last updated September 2023 (https refused, http answers); shillerdata.com's page exposes no plain link to the workbook. To bring it current: download ie_data.xls from shillerdata.com and put it at history/corporate/raw/SHILLER/ie_data.xls — the builder prefers it over ie_data_yale.xls

entries.title: Goyal and Welch, equity-premium predictor data (annual 1871-, updated yearly): dividends, earnings, book-to-market, net equity issuance, default and term spreads, inflation, stock variance
entries.retrieval: workflow: Amit Goyal's page (Google Sites) -> the Drive-hosted PredictorData workbook; if the link cannot be resolved, attach PredictorData<year>.xlsx under raw/GOYAL-WELCH/
entries.license: academic use with citation (Welch and Goyal 2008, RFS; Goyal, Welch and Zafirov 2024, RFS)
entries.provenance_class: compiled (CRSP, Shiller, FRED, Amit Goyal's own construction)
feeds: net equity issuance (ntis), book-to-market (bm), default yield spread (dfy, 1919-), stock variance (svar): counted corporate-finance variables with a crisis literature
entries.note: Data2025.xlsx supplied by hand 2026-11-06 (Amit Goyal's page, the 2025 edition, to 2025:12); corporate_build.py reads the Annual sheet and accepts the workbook's b/m spelling of book-to-market

entries.status: backfilled and re-reduced (desktop runs 2026-11-06/07): 71 sets 2009q1-2026q3 at aggregator v3
entries.title: SEC Financial Statement Data Sets: every number in 10-K/10-Q XBRL financial statements, quarterly 2009q1-
entries.retrieval: desktop (sec.gov refuses cloud addresses): every quarterly zip (20-120 MB) streamed and reduced; only aggregates kept (raw/SEC-FSDS/<yyyyqN>_aggregates.csv: per sector [all / nonfinancial / financial by SIC, v3], tag, qtrs and period end, the filer count, sum, median and p90 for assets, liabilities, equity, long-term debt, cash, inventories, revenue, net income, interest, operating cash flow, capex, buybacks, dividends, depreciation; 10-K/10-Q forms only, USD, no co-registrants, no dimensional rows, one value per filer from its latest-filed submission, values beyond a per-tag plausibility cap set aside; <yyyyqN>_meta.json: filing counts, values set aside, the five largest filers per large key, aggregator version)
entries.license: public domain (SEC); fair-access policy: identify the client in the User-Agent, at most 10 requests a second
entries.provenance_class: counted (self-reported, audited, as filed; restatements appear as later filings)
feeds: sec_fsds_quarterly.csv: per sector, period end and tag, filer count and sum for 3-month, year-to-date and annual rows (10-Q cash flows are year-to-date); the live dials' capex, buyback, dividend and cash read
sec_analysis.md/json: annual flows and ratios 2009-, the timely read, calibration against Z.1 and NIPA, the cross-file consistency check
entries.note: pulled from the owner's desktop with SEC_CONTACT set (the fair-access User-Agent); --all backfills, --redo re-reduces after an aggregator change (resumable by version), --selftest runs the synthetic checks; the first reduction's 'first value seen' took segment rows in the 10-K files (sums for the same date differed up to 2.1x across files); v3 keys values by filer, sets dimensional rows aside (220-340 thousand per set), splits sums by sector and caps implausible values (none found); the nonfinancial rows are the reads

entries.status: backfilled and re-reduced (desktop runs 2026-11-06/07): 54 of 54 sets 2013q2-Aug 2026 at aggregator v4; v5 (unit checked against the manager's history) applies from the next refresh
entries.title: SEC Form 13F Data Sets: institutional investment managers' quarterly holdings (long positions in 13(f) securities), structured from 2013q2
entries.coverage: managers with $100M+ in 13(f) securities, 2013-; 45-day filing lag
entries.retrieval: desktop (sec.gov refuses cloud addresses): every data-set zip (50-100 MB) streamed and reduced in two passes; only summaries kept (raw/SEC-13F/<period>_summary.json: report period, filings used and set aside, filers, total value in dollars, the set's unit and the filers found in the other unit, distinct issuers, top-10 and top-50 issuer shares, Herfindahl, median filer top-10 concentration, put/call share, aggregator version; <period>_top20.csv: the twenty most-held issuers)
entries.provenance_class: counted (self-reported, long-only, no shorts or most derivatives; VALUE in dollars from the filings made in 2023, thousands before, with filers that did not follow the form — detected per filer from the implied price of its lines, v2)
feeds: sec_13f_quarterly.csv: holdings date, filers, total value, issuers, top-10/top-50 issuer shares, Herfindahl, median filer top-10 concentration, put/call share, unit corrections; the positioning group's crowding read
sec_analysis.md/json: the concentration series against Z.1 corporate equities, with each period's status (current / provisional / stale)
entries.note: pulled from the owner's desktop with SEC_CONTACT set; the first aggregator scaled each set by its majority unit (filers in the other unit multiplied a thousandfold); v2-v4 (2026-11-07) detect the unit per filer, keep the set's own report-period filings, cap lines, filers and option books, apply curated exclusions (sec_13f_exclusions.csv) and list each set's two thousand largest managers; v5 checks a filer's unit against the manager's own history; corporate_build.py's audit over the manager lists writes sec_13f_flags.csv and the table's adjusted holdings value; the SEC serves the newest sets from /files/datastandardsinnovation/, which the puller tries beside the older paths
